edges.description: Atlastin GTPase activity is required for the homotypic ER fusion reaction, so its reduction directly impairs that fusion.
edges.source: Heterozygous ATL1 Variant with Reduced Atlastin-1 GTPase Activity

edges.description: Interconnection of ER tubules into a network depends on atlastin-mediated fusion, so impaired fusion disrupts the tubular network.

Defective ER morphogenesis is proposed to injure long, highly polarized neurons by interfering with proper membrane distribution or polarity; in HSN1D the vulnerable population is the long peripheral sensory axon. The intermediate steps between the ER-network defect and axonal degeneration are not established.
edges.target: Distal Degeneration of Long Sensory Axons

edges.source: Distal Degeneration of Long Sensory Axons

edges.description: Loss of protective sensation allows unperceived repetitive injury, which produces painless skin ulcers.
Unrecognized painless ulcers heal slowly and become infected, progressing to osteomyelitis that may necessitate distal amputation.
Mutant atlastin-1 prominently disrupts ER network morphology in COS-7 cells, recapitulating the ER-shaping defect at the cellular level.
edges.limitations: A non-neuronal heterologous overexpression system: it lacks the length-dependent axonal architecture of the human dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons that actually degenerate, so it cannot address the sensory-neuron-selective vulnerability, and overexpression may not reflect endogenous variant dosage.
edges.source: COS-7 heterologous expression of mutant atlastin-1

nodes.description: Loss of atlastin-mediated fusion disrupts the branched, interconnected tubular network of the peripheral endoplasmic reticulum. This ER-shaping defect is the cellular abnormality shared by the allelic disorders HSN1D and SPG3A, and the HSN1D mutant atlastin-1 prominently disrupts ER network morphology in cultured cells.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted high-throughput sequencing identifies mutations in atlastin-1 as a cause of hereditary sensory neuropathy type I.
evidence.snippet: The mutant protein exhibited reduced GTPase activity and prominently disrupted ER network morphology when expressed in COS7 cells, strongly supporting pathogenicity.

evidence.reference_title: Atlastin GTPases are required for Golgi apparatus and ER morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Abnormal morphogenesis of the ER and Golgi resulting from mutations in atlastin-1 may ultimately underlie SPG3A by interfering with proper membrane distribution or polarity of the long corticospinal motor neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary spastic paraplegia proteins REEP1, spastin, and atlastin-1 coordinate microtubule interactions with the tubular ER network.
evidence.snippet: the HSP proteins atlastin-1, spastin, and REEP1 interact within the tubularER membrane in corticospinal neurons to coordinate ER shaping and microtubule dynamics. Thus, defects in tubular ER shaping and network interactions with the microtubule cytoskeleton seem to be the predominant pathogenic mechanism of HSP.

nodes.description: The longest peripheral sensory axons, arising from dorsal root ganglion neurons, degenerate in a length-dependent axonal process, producing a sensory-predominant axonal neuropathy with variable axonal motor involvement. This reveals an unexpected major role for atlastin-1 in sensory neuron function.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted high-throughput sequencing identifies mutations in atlastin-1 as a cause of hereditary sensory neuropathy type I.
evidence.snippet: Hereditary sensory neuropathy type I (HSN I) is an axonal form of autosomal-dominant hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy distinguished by prominent sensory loss that leads to painless injuries.

nodes.description: HSN1D is caused by heterozygous dominant ATL1 variants (e.g. the missense p.Asn355Lys and p.Glu66Gln alleles and the p.Val326TrpfsX8 frameshift) that reduce the GTPase activity of atlastin-1, a large dynamin-related GTPase. Reduced GTPase activity is the shared molecular defect, and because the disease is dominant with truncating alleles among the mutations, both dominant-negative and haploinsufficiency effects have been proposed; the primary study demonstrated reduced GTPase activity and disrupted ER morphology for the mutant protein.
nodes.id: Heterozygous ATL1 Variant with Reduced Atlastin-1 GTPase Activity

evidence.reference_title: Targeted high-throughput sequencing identifies mutations in atlastin-1 as a cause of hereditary sensory neuropathy type I.
evidence.snippet: We detected a missense mutation (c.1065C>A, p.Asn355Lys) in atlastin-1 (ATL1), a gene that is known to be mutated in early-onset hereditary spastic paraplegia SPG3A and that encodes the large dynamin-related GTPase atlastin-1. The mutant protein exhibited reduced GTPase activity

evidence.reference_title: Structural basis for the nucleotide-dependent dimerization of the large G protein atlastin-1/SPG3A.
evidence.snippet: dimer formation in solution is observed only in the presence of GTP and transition state analogs, similar to other G proteins that are activated by nucleotide-dependent dimerization.

nodes.description: Atlastin-1 mediates GTP-dependent homotypic fusion of endoplasmic reticulum tubules; GTPase-deficient atlastin fails to self-associate into the trans-oligomeric complexes needed to tether and fuse apposed ER membranes, so mutant atlastin-1 cannot support the fusion reaction.

evidence.reference_title: Homotypic fusion of ER membranes requires the dynamin-like GTPase atlastin.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, GTPase-deficient Atlastin is inactive, unable to form trans-oligomeric complexes owing to failure to self-associate, and incapable of promoting fusion in vitro.

nodes.description: Meticulous foot and skin care, protective footwear, daily foot inspection, and early treatment of painless injuries to prevent ulceration, osteomyelitis, and amputation. Management follows diabetic-foot-care guidelines — removal of pressure from the ulcer and eradication of infection, followed by protective footwear.

evidence.snippet: Management of HSN I follows the guidelines given for diabetic foot care (removal of pressure to the ulcer and eradication of infection, followed by the use of specific protective footwear)
